$schema_note: Goal-evaluation tables shared by the LIBERO success predicates and the
metaworld-style dense reward. Suite-independent: keyed by asset, not by task.
articulation_joint_targets: per (asset, operation), the joint-position window
[low, high] that counts as the operation being satisfied, and the joint-name
pattern to match. Ranges are radians for revolute joints and metres for
prismatic ones, following each asset's own joint definition.
wooden_cabinet: the cabinet is layered, so its joint is chosen by the goal's
'layer' and its window by the operation, rather than by a single (asset,
operation) key.
orientation_offsets: positional offset [m] applied to a relationship goal's
target when the goal names a side ('put X to the right of Y').  These are
WORLD-frame (table-frame) offsets, as in the source BDDL -- unlike a goal's
'target_offset', which is asset-local and rotates with the target.
Signs and magnitudes are read off the source BDDL goal regions, which are
in the same table frame as the harvested init regions (verified: the
harvested pose_range values reproduce the BDDL ranges).
right: LIVING_ROOM_SCENE6 plate_right_region spans y in [0.05, 0.15]
about a plate at y ~ 0 -> +y, centre +0.10.  (plate_left_region is the
front: push_the_plate_to_the_front_of_the_stove stove_front_region is
centred at x = -0.05 while the stove spawns at x = -0.404 and the
burner-plate target_offset already carries +0.15 -> +0.204 from there.
These were both NEGATED before 2026-08-17, so 'right of the plate' scored
the LEFT side and 'front of the stove' a point 0.40 m past the stove;
libero_10 #6 and libero_goal #5 could not be satisfied at all.
Joint windows are bounded by each asset's USD limits.  The cabinet drawers
travel [-0.175, 0], so an 'open' window of [-0.16, -0.14] (the old white
cabinet value) scored a fully-pulled-out drawer as NOT open; both cabinets
now share [-0.175, -0.12] since they are the same USD.  The microwave door
and stove knob are authored with NO joint limits ((-inf, inf)) -- widening
their windows only mitigates that; the assets should get real limits.
These mirror the playground rl_utils tables
(_articulation_operation_goal_satisfied_by_group). They were Python dicts in
the reward module until they moved here; when comparing against playground,
diff these values against that function rather than against our source.
